deck_title: SpinDrift: Quantum Biosensors for Astronaut Health

slides.title: SpinDrift: Quantum Biosensors for Astronaut Health
slides.subtitle: Today's stations. Tomorrow's destinations.
slides.visual_direction: Dark deep-space backdrop with astronaut silhouette and three subtle glowing quantum sensor nodes on chest, head, and finger.
slides.speaker_notes: Introduce SpinDrift: continuous, consumable-free astronaut health monitoring built on three real quantum sensors and an environment-aware telemetry engine across today's orbital stations and tomorrow's deep-space destinations.

slides.title: The Problem
slides.headline: 180 days to Mars. No hospital. No lab.

current_limitations: Adhesive electrodes fail in sweat and irritate skin
Blood draws consume finite sterile supplies
mission_requirements: Real-time continuous cardiac, neural, and oxidative telemetry

slides.visual_direction: Split comparison card: Current (red-amber warning icons for electrodes, blood kits, liquid-helium dewar) vs Needed (green badges for wearable, real-time, zero consumables).
slides.speaker_notes: As missions leave low-Earth orbit for 180-day Mars transits and beyond, crews lose rapid return and resupply. The crew medical officer needs continuous telemetry without lab consumables.

slides.title: Three Quantum Sensors
slides.layout: One astronaut body diagram with three labeled sensor locations

sensors.label: Chest → OPM magnetocardiography (≈50 pT cardiac field)
sensors.primary_hardware: QuSpin QZFM OPM (⁸⁷Rb vapor cell, <15 fT/√Hz, domino-sized)
sensors.alternative_hardware: NV-diamond cardiac magnetometer (12 mm head, 6–26 pT/√Hz, measured real human hearts, arXiv 2601.18843, Jan 2026)

sensors.label: Head → OPM-MEG helmet (≈100 fT neural field, <7 fT/√Hz)
sensors.primary_hardware: Miniaturized OPM-MEG helmet (12 × 16.5 × 22.5 mm per sensor, <7 fT/√Hz, 130 Hz bandwidth, 0.7 W per head; 49–128 channels, FieldLine HEDscan class; wearable)

sensors.label: Finger → NV-diamond ROS sensing (5.3 × 10⁻¹³ M/√Hz)
sensors.primary_hardware: NV-diamond T₁ relaxometry (532 nm excitation, 637–800 nm readout, ROS sensitivity 5.3 × 10⁻¹³ M/√Hz; demonstrated in living cardiomyocytes)

slides.visual_direction: Single full-body astronaut schematic with callout lines to Chest (OPM MCG), Head (OPM-MEG helmet), and Finger (NV-diamond T₁ clip).
slides.speaker_notes: Every sensor in SpinDrift is grounded in demonstrated hardware: QuSpin QZFM (plus the Jan 2026 NV-diamond heart alternative), miniaturized 49–128 channel OPM-MEG helmets, and cardiomyocyte-demonstrated NV-diamond T₁ relaxometry.

slides.title: How They Work
slides.core_takeaway: All three use quantum spin states.

mechanisms.flow: Rb atoms and laser → spin precession → field readout
mechanisms.detail: Laser-polarized ⁸⁷Rb vapor precesses in proportion to cardiac (~50 pT) or neural (~100 fT) magnetic fields in the Spin-Exchange Relaxation-Free (SERF) regime.

mechanisms.flow: NV centers and 532 nm laser → radical magnetic noise → T₁ shortens → ROS index
mechanisms.detail: 532 nm excitation initializes NV spin states; paramagnetic free radicals shorten T₁ relaxation time, read out via 637–800 nm fluorescence as ROS index (T₁_baseline / T₁_current).

slides.visual_direction: Two clean horizontal physics pipelines converging on a shared badge: 'All three use quantum spin states.'
slides.speaker_notes: No electrodes touch sweat, and no blood leaves the body. Both sensor families read out biological signals through quantum spin state physics.

slides.title: Today vs Tomorrow

tomorrow.label: Europa
tomorrow.field_context: Jupiter ~420 µT field (OPMs degraded; rely on NV & surviving MEG)

tomorrow.label: Deep Space
tomorrow.field_context: <1 nT to few nT (peak SERF sensitivity, zero rescue)

sensitivity_bar.note: SERF OPM sensitivity improves as ambient magnetic field drops; Jupiter's ~420 µT field at Europa degrades OPMs while NV-diamond remains resilient.

slides.caption: The further from Earth's field, the better the sensors work — except near Jupiter.
slides.visual_direction: Two side-by-side columns (TODAY vs TOMORROW) above a qualitative OPM sensitivity bar showing sensitivity rising into Deep Space and dropping sharply at Europa (~420 µT).
slides.speaker_notes: Most medical hardware fights spaceflight. SERF OPMs benefit from space: as ambient field drops from LEO microteslas to deep-space nanoteslas, shielding vanishes and sensitivity peaks—until Europa, where Jupiter's ~420 µT field degrades OPMs and NV-diamond takes lead.

slides.title: Real Data
datasets: NASA OSDR OSD-580 — Spaceflight heart transcriptomics (NPPA cardiac wall-stretch signal)
NASA OSDR OSD-352 — Spaceflight hippocampus multiomics (BDNF / neurocognitive pathways)
OpenNeuro ds004902 — 71-subject sleep-deprivation EEG dataset (CC0; alpha/theta fatigue drift)
published_physiology: Renin rise (RAS activation under fluid shift)
slides.prototype_notice: Important: All environment-specific green/amber/red thresholds in SpinDrift are prototype hackathon thresholds — not clinically validated.
slides.caption: Every value traces to a dataset or a paper.
slides.visual_direction: Clean provenance grid linking OSDR/OpenNeuro dataset badges to each sensor channel, with a clear prototype disclaimer banner at the bottom.
slides.speaker_notes: We did not invent physiological trajectories. Cardiac and brain expression signals trace to OSDR OSD-580 and OSD-352, fatigue spectral drift traces to OpenNeuro ds004902, and fluid-shift biomarkers trace to Inspiration4 and published SANS literature. All alert thresholds are explicitly marked as prototype values, not clinically validated.

slides.title: What's Next
roadmap_items: Prototype a chest OPM patch (with NV-diamond high-field fallback)
Validate NV ROS sensing in a hypomagnetic chamber
Propose to Artemis crew health programs
Partner with an OPM-MEG manufacturer for a flight-qualified helmet
